newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to award eight mobile franchises Monday.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to award eight mobile franchises Monday.

text.p: Taiwan telecommunication officials said they had cut the field to 29 finalists in a high-stakes battle for eight lucrative mobile phone franchises and would announce the final winners later on Monday.
The names of the selected bidders would be disclosed at 1200 GMT, Ministry of Transport and Communications officials said.

The hotly contested bidding war was to have concluded in 1996 but Taipei has repeatedly called off planned announcements of its outcome, citing the need for further review of foreign ownership levels in the 42 complex applications.
Mobile telephony is one of several telecom sectors liberalised by parliament in January 1996, opening it up for private and limited foreign investments.

Seventeen joint ventures, some led by major international telecom firms, have submitted 42 applications to run the newly liberalised mobile telephone franchises that analysts say could yield up to US$3.6 billion a year in sales after 10 years.
Foreign investors can own stakes of up to 20 percent in Taiwan telecom ventures, though under some interpretations of the liberalised law foreigners can control up to 59 percent.

The foreign and domestic applicants include AT&T, Sprint Corp, Southwestern Bell and Air Touch of the United States, Hong Kong Telecommunications, Japan's Mitsubishi as well as Acer and the influential Koo's Group of Taiwan.
